candidates: The close() method stops the commit thread before shutting down the queue pool. With q.shutdown(immediate=False), workers continue processing remaining items in queues during queue_pool.shutdown(). Any offsets completed during this draining phase are marked complete via complete_offset() but never committed to Kafka because the commit thread has already exited. This can cause duplicate message processing on consumer restart.

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() shuts down the queue_pool that is owned by ResultsStrategyFactory. After a Kafka partition rebalance, create_with_partitions() reuses the same factory and passes the now-shut-down pool to a new strategy. The new strategy would attempt to submit work to dead worker threads and closed queues, causing the consumer to fail or hang after any rebalance event.
